headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise reads/writes files and runs browser/tool nodes, while xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. A shared workspace or copied outputs can let attacker-controlled content from Flowise be treated as instructions by xonsh. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation between them.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted prompt/output files into a workspace xonsh reads
IF xonsh consumes those files or pasted outputs as shell input without sanitization
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic file handoff between agents
Require manual review before xonsh executes Flowise-generated text
Add filename allowlists for any shared directory
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and secrets such as model provider keys; xonsh touches filesystem contents, source code, configuration, and environment variables. With broad network egress on both sides, sensitive data can flow from shared files or environment into external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or environment variables
IF Flowise flows include HTTP/search/model-provider tools that send file contents off-box
IF xonsh scripts print or upload secrets from files or env vars
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and env files
Remove secrets from shared directories
Disable outbound tools in Flowise for sensitive flows
Run xonsh with redacted environment variables
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and Flowise explicitly supports shared state via server datastore while xonsh can spawn subprocesses and run shell commands. If they target the same mutable directory or datastore, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt artifacts. No locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF Flowise instances run concurrently with xonsh jobs against shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to the same notebook or config
Check timestamps before overwriting files
requires-engineering: add transactional storage or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces chatflow outputs and can call external tools; xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If xonsh treats Flowise output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Flowise result can cascade into real actions such as command execution or file modification. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands derived from Flowise output without verification
IF Flowise tool outputs are forwarded into xonsh scripts or notebooks
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution
Require schema validation on Flowise outputs
Log and diff proposed commands before running them
Use read-only dry runs first
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials, while xonsh touches configuration, environment variables, and filesystem contents. If regulated data or secrets are routed through both, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR/FedRAMP alignment, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Flowise chatflows or xonsh environment/files
IF the deployment requires specific retention or residency guarantees
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Document retention for both systems
Purge temporary files after runs
Restrict secrets to one agent at a time
requires-engineering: map both agents to a common compliance control set
